key_insight: HARMONY combines semantic reasoning with geometric prediction to reconstruct a full 3D scene from a single image more accurately than either approach alone. It aims to preserve both object relationships and fine-grained reconstruction detail.
problem_solved: The paper addresses monocular image-to-scene synthesis: how to infer a complete 3D scene from one image while maintaining correct spatial relations between objects and high-fidelity geometry.
method: Uses hierarchical agentic reasoning to understand scene structure and inter-object spatial relationships.
Integrates visual geometry foundation model outputs for dense scene geometry prediction from the input image.
Fuses semantic reasoning and geometric cues to improve both alignment with the image and reconstruction quality.
impact: This is useful for AI/ML practitioners working on 3D vision, robotics, AR/VR, and scene understanding because it bridges the gap between semantic scene interpretation and precise geometric reconstruction. The approach suggests a stronger path toward reliable single-image 3D reconstruction.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing the input image split into reasoning and geometry branches, then merged into a 3D scene output.
A before-and-after comparison of reconstruction quality versus prior methods.
An icon-based illustration of objects and their spatial relationships in the scene.
A side-by-side visualization of semantic layout alignment and dense point-map prediction.
paper_title: HARMONY: Hierarchical Agentic Reasoning for MONocular Image-to-Scene Synthesis
paper_authors: Shufan Sun, Chen Wang, Enxin Song, Jiatao Gu, Lingjie Liu
